name: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (adult)

meta.title: GBM in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults; newly diagnosed and recurrent settings
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application showing how an in silico engine gates, models, and ranks treatment decisions across the GBM journey for clinicians, patients, and caregivers. Every claim resolves to a primary source; uncertainty is shown, not hidden; comfort care is always a modeled arm.
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.

Patient basics.label: age
Patient basics.help: Routes full-course vs short-course pathways (Perry 2017) and multiplies every anchor.
Patient basics.helpPatient: Age helps pick between longer and shorter radiation courses.

Patient basics.label: performance (KPS)
Patient basics.help: Prognostic modifier and hard gate: most trials and intensive arms require >=70/>=60.
Patient basics.helpPatient: How you are doing day to day - it decides which options are safe enough to help.

Patient basics.label: comorbidity burden
Patient basics.help: Shifts toxicity feasibility and burden more than survival estimates. Unknown is a gap, not a blank: CeTeG (lomustine + TMZ) carries a heavier haematologic toxicity profile, so fitness needs an actual…
Patient basics.helpPatient: Your other health conditions - they shape which side effects are acceptable risks.

Diagnostic gates.label: IDH status
Diagnostic gates.help: WHO CNS5 requires IDH-wildtype for the GBM diagnosis; mutant hard-reroutes to the astrocytoma pathway.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Tells us what disease this actually is. Everything else depends on this result.

Diagnostic gates.label: H3 status
Diagnostic gates.help: CNS5 also requires H3-wildtype; K27M reroutes to diffuse midline glioma (dordaviprone pathway); G34 reroutes to diffuse hemispheric glioma, H3 G34-mutant — a different disease.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: A second identity check on the tumor. A K27M result means a different disease and different options.

Diagnostic gates.label: MGMT promoter
Diagnostic gates.help: Single biggest ranking lever: predicts alkylator benefit, gates lomustine-TMZ, shifts the pseudoprogression prior. Assay method and cutoff matter — grey-zone results are 'indeterminate', which satisf…
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Tells us how well the main chemo is likely to work - the one result that changes the plan most.

Diagnostic gates.label: TERT promoter
Diagnostic gates.help: cIMPACT-NOW update 3 / WHO CNS5: in an IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytoma with lower-grade histology, TERT promoter mutation alone is sufficient for the molecular diagnosis of glioblastoma.

Diagnostic gates.label: Chromosome +7/−10
Diagnostic gates.help: Combined gain of chromosome 7 and loss of chromosome 10 — a second molecular criterion sufficient for molecular GBM (cIMPACT-NOW update 3; EGFR amplification is the third).

Diagnostic gates.label: 1p/19q codeletion
Diagnostic gates.help: 1p/19q codeletion defines oligodendroglioma — a hard reroute out of the GBM pathway. Intact codeletion status is part of confirming the astrocytic lineage.

Surgery & imaging.label: resection achieved
Surgery & imaging.help: Trial baselines were mostly debulked (Stupp 2005: 84% had debulking surgery), so gross total resection IS the anchor baseline and carries no extra multiplier — the prior x1.15 double-counted the same…
Surgery & imaging.helpPatient: How much tumor surgery removed - more removed gives every later treatment a better start.

Surgery & imaging.label: tumor location
Surgery & imaging.help: Drives the resectability call and predicted extent-of-resection scenario at Detection.
Surgery & imaging.helpPatient: Where the tumor sits decides how much surgery can safely do.

Surgery & imaging.label: imaging suggests lymphoma/mimic
Surgery & imaging.help: Trips the biopsy-first institutional rule; steroids held if safe (they can mask lymphoma).
Surgery & imaging.helpPatient: If the scan could be a lymphoma or a mimic, we biopsy first before any bigger surgery.

Surgery & imaging.label: focality
Surgery & imaging.help: Multifocal / multicentric disease or callosal crossing makes gross total resection unlikely regardless of eloquence - biopsy-first territory. Drives the resectability read, never a survival modifier.

Treatment context.label: steroid dose (dexamethasone)
Treatment context.help: Dexamethasone mg/day. Independent survival hazard (Pitter 2016) and a hard trial gate: EF-41 requires <=2 mg stable/decreasing; SURVIVE required <=4 mg. Dose and trend both matter - protect a steroid…
Treatment context.helpPatient: Steroid dose matters twice: people who need less tend to do better, and doses above 2 mg a day close immune-therapy doors. If swelling needs treating, ask about alternatives before higher steroid dos…

Treatment context.label: TTFields wear time
Treatment context.help: Scales the EF-14 anchor (x1.0 / x0.85 / x0.70) - the biggest modifiable factor for the device arm.
Treatment context.helpPatient: How many hours a day the scalp device is actually worn - the benefit follows the wear time.

Monitoring (on treatment).label: weeks post-chemoRT
Monitoring (on treatment).help: Sets the pseudoprogression timing prior (<=12 wks: high; 13-24: moderate; >24: low).
Monitoring (on treatment).helpPatient: How long since chemo-radiation finished - early scans often look worse without being worse.

Monitoring (on treatment).label: perfusion (rCBV)
Monitoring (on treatment).help: Strongest single discriminator in the is-it-working stage (x1.6 low / x0.45 high on the posterior).
Monitoring (on treatment).helpPatient: A blood-flow measurement that helps tell real growth from treatment inflammation.

Monitoring (on treatment).label: amino-acid PET
Monitoring (on treatment).help: Amino-acid PET sharpens the call when MRI is ambiguous (TBR 1.6 threshold, PET-RANO).
Monitoring (on treatment).helpPatient: A different kind of scan that can settle it when the MRI cannot decide.

Monitoring (on treatment).label: Response baseline scan
Monitoring (on treatment).help: RANO 2.0: in newly diagnosed disease the comparison baseline is the POST-RADIOTHERAPY MRI, not the post-operative scan. Using the wrong baseline miscalls response and progression.

Monitoring (on treatment).label: Confirmatory scan / histology obtained
Monitoring (on treatment).help: Inside 12 weeks of RT completion, RANO 2.0 requires a confirmatory MRI or tissue before progression can be declared. Also a trial fact: GBM AGILE excludes recurrent patients whose progression occurre…

Monitoring (on treatment).label: New lesion vs high-dose RT field
Monitoring (on treatment).help: A new/growing lesion inside the high-dose RT volume favors treatment effect (pseudoprogression); outside the field favors true tumor. One of the most discriminating single variables in the window.

Recurrence context.label: recurrence pattern
Recurrence context.help: Local vs diffuse gates repeat surgery and re-irradiation.
Recurrence context.helpPatient: Whether the recurrence is one focused spot or spread out - it decides if local options exist.

Recurrence context.label: months since first RT
Recurrence context.help: Opens or defers the re-irradiation window (>=6 months convention).
Recurrence context.helpPatient: Time since the first radiation course - repeat radiation usually waits at least six months.

Recurrence context.label: progression RANO-confirmed
Recurrence context.help: Two scans documenting progression against the post-RT baseline, or histology. Asserting recurrence without this trips the RANO hold; inside 12 weeks of chemoradiation it also violates the GBM AGILE e…

Recurrence context.label: prior lomustine exposure
Recurrence context.help: GBM AGILE's recurrent arm excludes any prior lomustine (registry verbatim) - and its randomized control IS lomustine. Choosing CeTeG or lomustine off-trial sets this flag forever.

Recurrence context.label: MMR / hypermutation at relapse
Recurrence context.help: Re-profile at relapse: TMZ-driven hypermutation / MMR deficiency argues against alkylator re-challenge and routes toward checkpoint-inhibitor trials.

Recurrence context.label: leptomeningeal spread
Recurrence context.help: Leptomeningeal dissemination changes the recurrence pathway (CSF-directed considerations, most focal options close) - flagged as a gate, never silently absorbed.

Molecular enrichment.label: NGS panel
Molecular enrichment.help: Actionable finds unlock arms live: BRAF V600E -> targeted; MMR-deficient -> checkpoint.
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: A full genetic profile. Usually confirms the plan; occasionally opens a door nobody knew was there.

Molecular enrichment.label: EGFRvIII / EGFR-amp assay
Molecular enrichment.help: Resolves CAR-T trial criteria (INCIPIENT; Penn bivalent).
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: A tumor test that can open specific CAR-T research studies.

Molecular enrichment.label: IL13Ra2 expression assay
Molecular enrichment.help: Resolves IL13Ra2 CAR-T criteria (Penn; City of Hope).
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: A tumor test that can open specific CAR-T research studies.

Molecular enrichment.label: survivin expression assay
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: A tumor test tied to one vaccine study.

Molecular enrichment.label: serial-MRI growth (D, rho)
Molecular enrichment.help: Two-timepoint D/rho estimate; modifies anchors (x1.08 slow / x0.88 fast) and calibrates the growth model.
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: Two scans taken apart in time let the model measure how this tumor actually grows.

Molecular enrichment.label: Ki-67 proliferation index
Molecular enrichment.help: Proliferation index; supports grading and growth priors but changes no available option in this trainer - do not delay a decision for it.
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: A microscope measurement of how fast cells divide. Interesting context, but it does not change any option here - no decision should wait for it.

Molecular enrichment.label: RNA-seq subtype
Molecular enrichment.help: Transcriptional class; mesenchymal applies a radioresistance penalty (x0.92). Enrichment, not gating.
Molecular enrichment.helpPatient: A deeper tumor-behavior profile - research-grade nuance rather than a decision-changer today.

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date.
Evidence-grade labels and single-arm/external-control caveats are never removed.
Comfort-focused care is always a modeled arm with real numbers, never a footnote.
Evidence reversals stay visible as teaching cases; reversed arms are never silently deleted.
Recurrence view carries the guideline no-recommendation banner.
Ranking is withheld, with the missing test named, when a tier-1 input is absent.
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper — stated in the footer.
When the model cannot distinguish two options, it says so instead of ranking them.
gates: idh must be wildtype for the GBM pathway
h3 must be wildtype for the GBM pathway
mgmt must be known before ranking frontline arms
lymphoma/mimic suspicion triggers biopsy before resection
high-dose steroids gate out checkpoint/CAR-T options
1p/19q must not be codeleted for the GBM pathway
lower-grade histology needs one of TERT / EGFR-amp / +7−10 for molecular GBM
hypermutation / MMR-deficiency at relapse cautions alkylator re-challenge
leptomeningeal spread changes the recurrence pathway
care: NCI-designated center / multidisciplinary neuro-oncology tumor board
